newsitem.title: USA: USAir will not buy back BA's stake.
newsitem.headline: USAir will not buy back BA's stake.

text.p: USAir Group Inc said Tuesday it will not exercise its right to buy back British Airways Plc's 24.6 percent stake in USAir.

USAir spokesman Rick Weintraub declined to comment on whether USAir decided against buying the shares or was restricted by a Delaware Capital Surplus law which limits share repurchases unless a company meets certain capital surplus requirements.

While BA is now free to sell its stake in private transactions or a public offering, it is restricted from selling the shares in one lump. Under an agreement with USAir, BA cannot sell its stake to any entity that would gain more than five percent of USAir's stock.
BA was not immediately available to comment on its plans.

BA said in December it planned to sell its 24.6 percent stake in USAir at a premium to its original investment of $400 million. Three of BA's directors resigned from USAir's board in January as the two carriers continued to dismantle a turbulent relationship that began in 1993.
BA and USAir began feuding publicly last summer after BA proposed a broad alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines.

USAir sued BA in July, alleging the proposed BA-American deal undermined the existing relationship between USAir and BA. USAir also contends that the proposed deal would allow BA and American to monopolize air travel between the United States and Britain.
